Series::StatAccessor::kurtosis¶

Back to Series::StatAccessor API Reference

Signatures¶

Series Series::StatAccessor::kurtosis() const
Series Series::StatAccessor::kurtosis(std::int64_t dim) const
Series SeriesStatProxy::kurtosis() const
Series SeriesStatProxy::kurtosis(std::int64_t dim) const

What It Does¶

kurtosis() reports excess kurtosis, a standardized fourth-moment summary. The normal-distribution reference is therefore 0, not Pearson kurtosis 3. Positive values indicate heavier-tail or sharper-peak behavior relative to that reference; negative values indicate flatter or lighter-tail behavior.

This is a reduction and a shape descriptor, not a spread measurement. Two lanes can have different scales or asymmetries and still share the same kurtosis.

Parameters And Returns¶

Omitting dim pools the complete owner. Supplying dim, including a negative dimension, computes one value per surviving lane. The global result currently has shape [1].

Examples¶

Example 1. Symmetric three-point rows produce negative excess kurtosis.

auto symmetric = pluss::make_series({1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, {2, 3});
std::cout << symmetric.stat.kurtosis(1) << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[-1.5, -1.5]

Example 2. These lopsided rows have the same fourth-moment summary despite their nonzero skewness.

auto lopsided = pluss::make_series({1, 1, 4, 2, 2, 8}, {2, 3});
std::cout << lopsided.stat().kurtosis(1) << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[-1.5, -1.5]

Example 3. Pooling changes the population and therefore the fourth moment.

std::cout << lopsided.stat.kurtosis() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[1], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=[0.055555556]

The symmetric and lopsided rows share kurtosis even though their skewness differs. Kurtosis and skewness are separate questions, not interchangeable measures of distribution irregularity. Pooling also changes the result.

Interpretation Limits¶

Kurtosis is highly sensitive to rare extremes and unstable on short lanes. Use it as descriptive evidence alongside counts, quantiles, and skewness rather than as a complete statement about distribution shape.
